Admissions

Advisors accept most applications themselves. These three are here because they are Private Mandates, or because an advisor was not certain — and a principal takes the uncertain ones.

148Applications this year
46Accepted
102Declined, with a reason given
31%Acceptance rate

Application 2608-14 · reviewed by C. Vasseur · Private Mandate

Publicly recognised. Wants a search nobody can know is happening.

Your decision

C. Vasseur recommends acceptance and says she can run it. The complication is not the member — it is that a search this quiet needs two advisors who never discuss it with anyone, and we have three mandates already running on that footing. Her question is whether the house has the capacity to keep a fourth genuinely silent.

Application 2608-09 · reviewed by R. Sole · Signature

Referred by a member. The advisor would decline.

Your decision

R. Sole's note: "He describes what he wants entirely in terms of what she should look like and where she should have studied. I asked twice about temperament and got nothing back. I do not think we can serve him and I do not think he would take our answer well." The complication is who referred him — a member of nine years. Declining is right; it should come from a principal, not from R. Sole.

Application 2608-11 · reviewed by K. Marsh · Reserve

Straightforward, except the city.

Your decision

Milan. We have no advisor there and no correspondent yet. K. Marsh can run the assessment and would need a correspondent for the search itself, or the member should be told plainly that we are not the right house for a Milan-only brief.

Every decline is written to the applicant by a person, with a reason. We do not send form letters and we have never charged for an application.

Conduct

An advisor can end a contact, arrange transport, and record a report the same day. What they cannot do is remove someone from the network. That decision is a principal's, and it is written down with your name on it.

Escalated 19 August by C. Vasseur · reported by S. Lindqvist

Removal from the network

Unanswered · 14 hours

She reported that he pressed about money in a way she found calculated, and did not stop when she twice changed the subject. Contact was ended the same day and she was told so. This is the second report about him — the first, in March, was a different member and was recorded but not acted on.

Reports
Two, from unconnected members
She asked for
End all contact · not to be named
His engagement
Reserve, commenced February
Fee
Settled. Not returned on removal

March · recorded, not acted on

The earlier report about the same member

Closed at the time

A single account, no pattern, and the member did not want anything done. The house recorded it and left it. With a second report from an unconnected member, that judgment looks different — which is the reason we record the ones we do not act on.

What a removal means

  • The engagement ends. The fee is not returned.
  • The other party is told what the house has done, and why.
  • The reporting member is never named to anyone.
  • The decision is recorded against a principal's name, permanently.
  • Readmission requires two principals, and has never been granted.

What we do not do

  • No fee contingent on an introduction, a meeting, or a marriage.
  • No monthly billing and no automatic renewal — a renewal is a conversation.
  • No charge for an application, ever.
  • No commission paid to or taken from a correspondent for introducing a person.
  • No fee returned on removal for conduct.

The wall between services

  • A lookup never reveals whether the holder is a member.
  • Identity holders are not approached about the practice. Not once.
  • Member files and mark records are held separately.
  • 23 of 212 holders are members — and no one checking a code can tell which.

Standards that are not settings

Two principals to change

Every candidate is met in person before being proposed

Turning this off would make us an introduction service. It has never been off.

Consent is asked separately for every disclosure

The consent ledger depends on it, and so does everything we tell members about privacy.

A case cannot be sent without a second advisor's disagreement

Five conditions on the compose screen. Removing one would be the fastest way to lower the standard invisibly.

No public profiles, directory or browsing

The absence is the product. There is no version of this house with a member list.

These are shown as switches to make a point: they are the four things that could be switched off quietly and would destroy the house within a year. They require two principals, a written reason, and the reason is published to every member.
